**Analysis of test image vs references:**

The test image shows:
- A tomato plant on **black plastic mulch with wire trellis** — identical growing system to the Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference (Bugwood_2, #5593847)
- A large, elongated **brown/gray stem canker** as the focal point
- **Dark spots** embedded in the stem lesion (consistent with Sclerotinia sclerotia)
- Complete **plant collapse** — all leaves above the lesion are dead/brown
- Green algae on the stem indicating high moisture environment

**Comparison to candidates:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Reference showed nearly identical setting (black plastic, wire trellis), similar plant collapse pattern, and stem girdling lesion. Sclerotinia causes tan-to-brown stem cankers with black sclerotia (the dark spots visible on the stem match this well). Strong match.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Reference was microscopic — not useful for field comparison, but the dark spots on a stem lesion are consistent. Less certainty.
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt**: Reference showed leaf marginal necrosis/scorching — doesn't match the stem canker focus of the test image.
- **Gray_Mold**: Reference was microscopic; Gray_Mold (Botrytis) typically shows fuzzy gray sporulation — not clearly visible in test image.

The combination of stem girdling canker + dark spots (likely sclerotia) + whole-plant death above the lesion + identical black plastic/wire trellis system strongly points to Sclerotinia Timber Rot.
